Axis 4-7 verdict-COMPOSED claims follow MIN_PRECEDENCE rule\n# === TIER-3 local codification provenance ===\n# TIER-3 local: this rule was codified Wave 123 fire 1 in response to user directive 2026-05-09 (\"kits v1-v65 are INSPIRATION not source-of-truth — improve SOTA-definition to be discoverable INDEPENDENT of kit curation\"). cite-class effective_tier=TIER-3-LOCAL-COMPOSITION per CR-1 + CR-8 lattice (sibling-novel discipline; no upstream parity for Axes 4-7 multi-axis-leadership framework).\n\n## The thesis\n\nSOTA is **discoverable from FIRST-PRINCIPLES across the discovery surface**, NOT from any single curation. Curated lists (kits / awesome-* / vendor-marketing-pages) are INSPIRATION sources at best — they reflect the curator's selection bias and update cadence, neither of which is a substitute for first-principles convergence verification.\n\nWave 122 fire 1 surfaced the kit-curation anchor antipattern: Agent A+D treated \"n=7 universal-tier in kits = definitive SOTA\" — over-anchoring on kit author's selections rather than triangulating across independent discovery surfaces. This rule replaces that with a 7-axis framework: Axes 1+2+3 (FLOOR — convergence-gate inherits) + Axes 4-7 (LEADERSHIP — newness / adversarial-filter / benchmark-provenance / architectural-novelty).\n\n## The 7 axes (FLOOR + LEADERSHIP)\n\n### FLOOR — Axes 1+2+3 (convergence-gate authority; do NOT duplicate mechanics here)\n\n| Axis | Threshold | Owner rule |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Axis 1 — independent T1 sources** | ≥3 distinct orgs/repos/papers implementing the pattern | `convergence-gate.md:18` |\n| **Axis 2 — named T2 practitioners** | ≥2 named practitioners with dated artifact citing THIS specific pattern | `convergence-gate.md:21` |\n| **Axis 3 — stability** | ≥3 months from earliest public artifact (cpd × age 5-band table; STRONG-PROVENANCE-EXPRESS predicate at age ≥30d if axis-1 official-org + axis-2 named-T2 endorsement) | `convergence-gate.md:22,94-104` |\n\nAny axis failing = REJECT-until-convergence. This is the **necessary** floor — Axes 4-7 below add **leadership** detection beyond the floor. A candidate that passes Axes 1+2+3 but fails Axes 4-7 is convergence-VALID but NOT SOTA-LEADERSHIP.\n\n### LEADERSHIP — Axes 4-7 (this rule's contribution)\n\n### Axis 4 — NEWNESS-LEADERSHIP (necessary not sufficient)\n\n**Definition**: candidate is published OR substantively updated within last 60 days AND demonstrates a NEW MECHANISM (not merely \"newer than X\").\n\n**Probe**:\n1. GitHub recency filter: `mcp__github__search_repositories sort:updated date:>YYYY-MM-DD` (replace YYYY-MM-DD with `today - 60d`)\n2. arxiv recency filter: `mcp__arxiv__search_papers` with date-range filter\n3. Cross-ref vs incumbent primitives: enumerate `Z:/claude-sota-installed/.claude/hooks/scripts/` + `docs/sota-installed-manifest.md` + sibling `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/` for existing primitive coverage\n4. **Mechanism test**: candidate must REPLACE OR AUGMENT a primitive class (NOT just \"ship faster than incumbent\" / \"rename incumbent's API\" / \"vendor-fork of incumbent\")\n\n**Threshold**: novelty must replace OR augment a primitive class. \"Newer-than-X\" alone is INSUFFICIENT — Axis 4 is necessary but NOT sufficient (must corroborate with Axis 5+6+7).\n\n**Anti-pattern**: dating-by-fork-creation. A repo created 2026-05-08 that's a fork of a 2024-01-01 incumbent does NOT pass Axis 4 — earliest public artifact controls per `convergence-gate.md:97` (\"first commit / first public post date\"). cite-anchor: `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/convergence-gate.md:97`.\n\n### Axis 5 — ADVERSARIAL-FILTER (cross-model challenge survives)\n\n**Definition**: candidate survives cross-model adversarial review when given the incumbent set + candidate as input.\n\n**Probe**:\n1. Dispatch Path P codex T1 with adversarial-mode prompt template (per `cross-model-consensus.md §\"T1-T7 touchpoint lifecycle\"` T1 row; Phase 1 bootstrap exception applies — orchestrator-side `codex exec` foreground+tee acceptable per CR-3)\n2. Prompt structure: `\"Given incumbents [list with file:line cites] AND candidate [cite + claim], emit one of three verdicts: (a) candidate dethrones incumbent X (cite which axis), (b) candidate adds non-overlapping primitive Y (name the primitive class), (c) candidate REJECT-FOR-FIT (cite which Probe DAG axis fails)\"`\n3. **Threshold**: cross-model verdict ≥0.85 conf with VERDICT shape `(a)` OR `(b)`. Verdict `(c)` triggers REJECT-UNTIL-CONVERGENCE re-evaluation\n4. **Cross-model invariant**: codex GPT-5.5 verdict origin REQUIRED — Sonnet stand-in does NOT satisfy Axis 5 per `cross-model-consensus.md §\"Env-funneled subagent stand-in disclosure mandate\"`. STAND-IN-NOTICE verdicts are AXIS-5-FAIL by definition (cross-model gate not satisfied)\n\n**Mandatory FM-09 carve-out**: 2nd-stage validator MUST NOT be `codex-rescue` (same blind-spot per `agent-harness-fit-verification.md` FM-09 specialization L103-130). Use `sota-researcher` / `architect` / orchestrator-direct codex T1 dispatch instead.\n\n**Iron Law**: Axis 5 verdict carries verbatim quote + file:line evidence from candidate AND incumbents — no paraphrase per `superpowers/verification-before-completion/SKILL.md:1-20` Iron Law \"verify EVIDENCE before claims\".\n\n### Axis 6 — BENCHMARK-PROVENANCE (reproducible scorecard)\n\n**Definition**: candidate cites a reproducible benchmark scorecard, NOT vendor-marketing claims.\n\n**Probe**:\n1. Locate benchmark surface: separate eval repo (e.g., `gbrain-evals` companion to `gbrain`) OR inline `BENCHMARK.md` with fixtures + repro commands\n2. Apply `convergence-gate.md §\"Anti-pattern: Row-2 fabrication-test FAIL\"` 3-tier evidence-density ladder:\n   - **Tier 0** (auto-FAIL): ≥3 README numeric claims lack live methodology artifact (no benchmark script path / dataset name / tool+version) — REJECT\n   - **Tier 1** (mega-exemplar): dedicated eval repo with versioned scorecards (e.g., `garrytan/gbrain-evals` precedent at `convergence-gate.md` §exemplar)\n   - **Tier 2** (strong-PASS): inline `BENCHMARK.md` with ≥21 fixtures + repro instructions (e.g., `context-mode/BENCHMARK.md` precedent)\n3. Per-numeric-claim audit: for each performance assertion in candidate's README, verify cite to reproducible artifact. ≥3 unsourced claims = AUTO-FAIL per fabrication-test rule\n4. **Threshold**: candidate must reach Tier 1 OR Tier 2. Tier 0 = REJECT (do NOT spend live A/B verification budget — prior probability of \"≥3 unsourced yet verifiable\" is empirically near-zero per sibling `convergence-gate.md` §3-tier ladder)\n\n**Anti-pattern carve-out**: benchmark-PRESENT-but-vendor-cherry-picked = HONEST-NON-FINDING per `synthesis-layer-verify.md §\"Reporting categories\"`. Vendor benchmarks comparing only against weak baselines fail Axis 6 even at Tier-2 evidence-density (cherry-picked methodology violates the spirit of reproducibility).\n\n### Axis 7 — ARCHITECTURAL-NOVELTY (genuinely new mechanism shape)\n\n**Definition**: primitive shape is NOT covered by current installed surface OR sibling rule catalog.\n\n**Probe** (cross-ref against existing primitive surfaces):\n1. **Hook surface**: enumerate `Z:/claude-sota-installed/.claude/hooks/scripts/` (when populated post-Tier-1a install) + sibling `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/hooks/scripts/` + Anthropic-CC official hook events at `https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks`\n2. **Manifest surface**: `Z:/claude-sota-installed/docs/sota-installed-manifest.md` §0..§17 install-class enumeration\n3. **Failure-mode catalog**: sibling `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/named-failure-modes.md` FM-01..FM-20 — does candidate address a NEW failure-mode class?\n4. **Lifecycle stage**: cross-ref vs `cross-model-consensus.md` T0-T7 lifecycle — does candidate add a NEW touchpoint OR new gate type?\n5. **Data structure**: does candidate introduce NEW data structure for cross-model consensus (e.g., new verdict-shape, new audit-trail JSONL schema, new permission-decision primitive)?\n\n**Threshold**: candidate must demonstrate genuinely new mechanism. Acceptable shapes:\n- NEW failure-mode class (FM-21+ candidate per `named-failure-modes.md` jurisdiction)\n- NEW lifecycle stage (T8+ candidate per `cross-model-consensus.md` T-touchpoint enumeration)\n- NEW gate type (e.g., post-deploy production-audit gate, pre-merge cumulative review)\n- NEW data structure for cross-model consensus\n\n**Anti-pattern**: \"incremental optimization of incumbent\" — making an incumbent 10% faster does NOT pass Axis 7. Axis 7 requires SHAPE novelty, not magnitude novelty.\n\n**Probe DAG dependency**: Axis 7 depends on `agent-harness-fit-verification.md` Probe 4 (plugin-namespace) + Probe 5 (mode-harness-shape) PASS — if candidate duplicates an existing plugin-loaded primitive OR requires unmet harness/mode assumption, Axis 7 FAILS regardless of mechanism novelty.\n\n## Cross-curation triangulation (mandatory; the kit-debias mechanism)\n\nEvery candidate MUST appear in **≥2 INDEPENDENT curations** before SOTA classification. Single-curation = REJECT-UNTIL-CONVERGENCE per `convergence-gate.md` Axis 1 ≥3-distinct-orgs requirement extended to discovery surface.\n\n**Acceptable independent-curation shapes**:\n1. **GitHub HEAD repo** (the implementation itself, with axis-1+2+3 floor passing)\n2. **arxiv paper** (peer-reviewed OR preprint) citing the pattern with named-T2 author\n3. **Anthropic OFFICIAL marketplace** (`/plugin install` from `https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official`) — TIER-1-DIRECT canonical\n4. **Named-T2 endorsement** (Karpathy / Boris Cherny / obra / Addy Osmani / equivalent named-author dated artifact)\n5. **Independent benchmark scorecard** (Axis 6 evidence — separate eval repo OR `BENCHMARK.md`)\n6. **CCBP authority** (`Z:/repos/deps/claude-code-best-practice-shan/` cite at file:line @ HEAD SHA — NOT a kit, but a structured upstream best-practice reference)\n\n**Independence test**: two curations are INDEPENDENT iff they have NO shared maintainer / authoring-org / direct-fork relationship. Examples:\n- GitHub repo + Anthropic OFFICIAL marketplace = INDEPENDENT (different orgs)\n- Two awesome-lists curated by the same author = NOT INDEPENDENT (same maintainer)\n- Repo + its README's self-cited \"Praise from users\" section = NOT INDEPENDENT (same source)\n- Repo + arxiv paper by same author = NOT INDEPENDENT (same author) — third curation required\n\n**Triangulation discipline**: log each curation in `docs/install-provenance.md` with shape + source URL + verification evidence. Single-curation candidates surface as `STAGED-AWAITING-CURATION-2` rows pending second-curation discovery.\n\n## Anti-patterns (5 codified)\n\n1. **\"Curated list = SOTA\"** — refuted by Wave 122 kits framing pivot. Kits v1-v65 represent curator-selection-bias snapshot at a fixed timestamp; SOTA is discoverable INDEPENDENT of any single curator. Kit appearance is INSPIRATION evidence (one curation among required ≥2), NOT definitive SOTA.\n\n2. **\"Star-count = SOTA\"** — refuted by `convergence-gate.md` Axis 3 5-band table. A 99-day-old repo at cpd>50 with 10K stars in `unknown-org + age<100d` band = LAUNCH-SPIKE anti-pattern (REJECT-UNTIL-CONVERGENCE). High stars correlate with attention, not correctness — see `convergence-gate.md` §\"Even-shorter-path: upstream self-flags impostor-domain risk\".\n\n3. **\"Recently-published = SOTA\"** — refuted at this rule's Axis 4 threshold. Newness is necessary but NOT sufficient — Axis 4 must corroborate with Axis 5 (adversarial-filter) AND Axis 6 (benchmark-provenance) AND Axis 7 (architectural-novelty). A 30-day-old repo with no benchmark + no adversarial-review + duplicates incumbent = AXIS-4-PASS-but-NOT-SOTA.\n\n4. **\"Vendor-claims = SOTA\"** — refuted by Axis 6 + `convergence-gate.md` §Row-2 fabrication-test. ≥3 unsourced numeric claims in vendor README = AUTO-FAIL. Vendor cherry-picked benchmarks at Tier-2 evidence-density still fail (cherry-picked methodology violates spirit of reproducibility).\n\n5. **\"Single-curation = SOTA\"** — refuted by §Cross-curation triangulation above. Any candidate appearing in only ONE curation surface = REJECT-UNTIL-CONVERGENCE. The kit-debias mechanism is operationalized at this level: discovery surface MUST include ≥2 INDEPENDENT curations.\n\n## Application discipline (the workflow)\n\nBefore declaring a candidate SOTA in any artifact (`docs/sota-installed-manifest.md` install row / commit body / rule-edit cite):\n\n1. **Floor check**: run convergence-gate Axes 1+2+3 — fail any = REJECT\n2. **Cross-curation triangulation**: ≥2 INDEPENDENT curations — fail = REJECT-UNTIL-CONVERGENCE\n3. **Axis 4 (NEWNESS-LEADERSHIP)**: <60d AND new mechanism — fail = candidate is convergent-classic, not SOTA-LEADERSHIP\n4. **Axis 5 (ADVERSARIAL-FILTER)**: cross-model verdict (a) OR (b) at ≥0.85 conf — fail = AXIS-5-FAIL, do NOT ship\n5. **Axis 6 (BENCHMARK-PROVENANCE)**: Tier 1 OR Tier 2 evidence-density — fail = REJECT\n6. **Axis 7 (ARCHITECTURAL-NOVELTY)**: genuinely new shape — fail = candidate is incremental-improvement, not SOTA-LEADERSHIP\n\nOutput verdict shape: `SOTA-LEADERSHIP-CONFIRMED` (all 7 axes PASS) / `CONVERGENT-CLASSIC` (Axes 1+2+3 PASS, Axes 4-7 partial) / `REJECT-UNTIL-CONVERGENCE` (any axis fails) / `HONEST-NON-FINDING` (probe budget exhausted before classification).\n\n## Related rules\n\n- `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/convergence-gate.md` — Axis 1+2+3 floor authority (mechanics owner; This is the **necessary** floor — Axes 4-7 below add **leadership** detection beyond the floor. A candidate that passes Axes 1+2+3 but fails Axes 4-7 is convergence-VALID but NOT SOTA-LEADERSHIP.\\n\\n### LEADERSHIP — Axes 4-7 (this rule's contribution)\\n\\n### Axis 4 — NEWNESS-LEADERSHIP (necessary not sufficient)\\n\\n**Definition**: candidate is published OR substantively updated within last 60 days AND demonstrates a NEW MECHANISM (not merely \\\"newer than X\\\").\\n\\n**Probe**:\\n1. A repo created 2026-05-08 that's a fork of a 2024-01-01 incumbent does NOT pass Axis 4 — earliest public artifact controls per `convergence-gate.md:97` (\\\"first commit / first public post date\\\"). cite-anchor: `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/convergence-gate.md:97`.\\n\\n### Axis 5 — ADVERSARIAL-FILTER (cross-model challenge survives)\\n\\n**Definition**: candidate survives cross-model adversarial review when given the incumbent set + candidate as input.\\n\\n**Probe**:\\n1. Vendor benchmarks comparing only against weak baselines fail Axis 6 even at Tier-2 evidence-density (cherry-picked methodology violates the spirit of reproducibility).\\n\\n### Axis 7 — ARCHITECTURAL-NOVELTY (genuinely new mechanism shape)\\n\\n**Definition**: primitive shape is NOT covered by current installed surface OR sibling rule catalog.\\n\\n**Probe** (cross-ref against existing primitive surfaces):\\n1. **Hook surface**: enumerate `Z:/claude-sota-installed/.claude/hooks/scripts/` (when populated post-Tier-1a install) + sibling `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/hooks/scripts/` + Anthropic-CC official hook events at `https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks`\\n2. **Manifest surface**: `Z:/claude-sota-installed/docs/sota-installed-manifest.md` §0..§17 install-class enumeration\\n3. **Failure-mode catalog**: sibling `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/named-failure-modes.md` FM-01..FM-20 — does candidate address a NEW failure-mode class?\\n4. **Lifecycle stage**: cross-ref vs `cross-model-consensus.md` T0-T7 lifecycle — does candidate add a NEW touchpoint OR new gate type?\\n5. **Data structure**: does candidate introduce NEW data structure for cross-model consensus (e.g., new verdict-shape, new audit-trail JSONL schema, new permission-decision primitive)?\\n\\n**Threshold**: candidate must demonstrate genuinely new mechanism. Acceptable shapes:\\n- NEW failure-mode class (FM-21+ candidate per `named-failure-modes.md` jurisdiction)\\n- NEW lifecycle stage (T8+ candidate per `cross-model-consensus.md` T-touchpoint enumeration)\\n- NEW gate type (e.g., post-deploy production-audit gate, pre-merge cumulative review)\\n- NEW data structure for cross-model consensus\\n\\n**Anti-pattern**: \\\"incremental optimization of incumbent\\\" — making an incumbent 10% faster does NOT pass Axis 7. exhausted accounts trigger emergency fallback\n- **Quota Protection**: Set minimum quota levels globally, per-account, or per-model to switch accounts before quota runs out\n- **Emergency Fallback**: When all accounts appear exhausted, bypasses checks with throttle delays (250-500ms)\n- **Automatic Cooldown**: Rate-limited accounts recover automatically after reset time expires\n- **Invalid Account Detection**: Accounts needing re-authentication are marked and skipped\n- **Prompt Caching Support**: Session IDs derived from conversation enable cache hits across turns\n\n## Monitoring\n\nCheck account status, subscription tiers, and quota anytime:\n\n```bash\n# Web UI: http://localhost:8080/ (Accounts tab - shows tier badges and quota progress)\n# CLI Table:\ncurl \"http://localhost:8080/account-limits?format=table\"\n```\n\n### CLI Management Reference\n\nIf you prefer using the terminal for management:\n\n```bash\n# List all accounts\nantigravity-claude-proxy accounts list\n\n# Verify account health\nantigravity-claude-proxy accounts verify\n\n# Interactive CLI menu\nantigravity-claude-proxy accounts\n```\n\n```\n\n---\n\nTitle: israads/claude-multisession\nURL: https://github.com/israads/claude-multisession\nPublished: 2026-02-28T02:38:51.000Z\nAuthor: N/A\nHighlights:\nRun multiple Claude Code instances simultaneously, each logged into a different account. That means:\n[...]\n- You can only be logged into **one account at a time**\n- Switching accounts means logging out and back in\n- You lose conversation context when switching\n- You can't run two sessions with different accounts in parallel\n[...]\nIf you have a personal account and a work account, or multiple clients each with their own org — you're stuck constantly logging in and out.\n[...]\n`claude-multisession` creates isolated session directories. Each session has its own authentication and history, but they all share your settings, MCP servers, and plugins. You log in once per session, and it stays logged in forever.\n[...]\n### You want to maximize rate limits\n[...]\nClaude Code has per-account rate limits. With multiple accounts on different plans, you can keep working when one hits its limit.\n[...]\n```bash\nclauded-1    # → account A (hit rate limit)\nclauded-2    # → account B (still has capacity) — keep working\n```\n[...]\nTwo developers, one workstation. Each has their own Claude account.\n[...]\nIndependent history, independent auth, independent billing.\n[...]\nmix up context\n[...]\nEach session remembers its login. Next time you run `clauded-1`, you're already authenticated — no need to log in again.\n[...]\n| --- | --- |\n| `clauded\n[...]\n) |\n[...]\n|\n| `clauded! 1\n[...]\n(skip prompts) |\n| `\n[...]\nsession |\n| `\n[...]\n|\n|\n[...]\n|\n|\n[...]\n|\n|\n[...]\n## How it works\n[...]\n```\n~/.claude/                  ← your global config (shared)\n[...]\n~/.claude-sessions/         ← created by multisession\n  ├── default/              ← clauded / clauded-0\n  │   ├── auth/             ← independent login (chmod 700)\n  │   ├── history.jsonl     ← independent conversations\n  │   ├── projects/         ← independent project memory\n  │   ├── settings.json     ← symlink → ~/.claude/settings.json\n  │   └── plugins           ← symlink → ~/.claude/plugins\n  ├── session-1/            ← clauded-1\n  │   ├── auth/             ← different account\n  │   ├── history.jsonl     ← different conversations\n  │   └── ...\n  └── session-2/            ← clauded-2\n      └── ...\n```\n[...]\n**Isolated per session:** authentication, conversation history, project memory, cache.\n[...]\n**Shared across sessions (configurable):** settings.json, MCP servers, plugins, IDE config. On first launch of each session, you choose whether to share (symlink) or copy (independent).\n[...]\n```bash\nPERMISSIONS_MODE=\"default\"   # \"default\" or \"full\"\nSESSION_COUNT=\"5\"            # number of sessions\nSHARING_MODE=\"shared\"        # \"shared\", \"independent\", or \"ask\"\nCMD_NAME=\"clauded\"           # your chosen command name\n[...]\n| Setting | Options | What it controls |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `PERMISSIONS_MODE` | `default` / `full` | Whether Claude asks before risky operations |\n| `SHARING_MODE` | `shared` / `independent` / `ask` | Whether sessions share settings from `~/.claude` or get their own copy |\n| `CMD_NAME` | any name | The command you type to launch sessions |\n[...]\nPer-session overrides are stored in `~/.claude-sessions/ /.cms-session-config`.\n\n---\n\nTitle: Multi-Account Load Balancing | badrisnarayanan/antigravity-claude-proxy | DeepWiki\nURL: https://deepwiki.com/badrisnarayanan/antigravity-claude-proxy/3.2-multi-account-load-balancing\nPublished: 2026-01-07T11:16:40.000Z\nAuthor: N/A\nHighlights:\nLast indexed: 7 January 2026 (992fa7)\n[...]\nThis document describes the multi-account load balancing system implemented by the `AccountManager` class and its subsystems. The load balancer manages a pool of Google accounts, intelligently distributes requests across them, tracks per-model rate limits, and automatically switches accounts when quota is exhausted.\n[...]\nThe `AccountManager` class (src/account-manager/index.js) serves as the central coordinator for multi-account operations. It is structured as a facade that delegates to specialized sub-modules:\n[...]\n|Module|Responsibility|Key Functions|\n|**Storage**|Load/save account configuration from `accounts.json`|`loadAccounts()`, `saveAccounts()`|\n|**Selection**|Choose which account to use for each request|`pickNext()`, `selectAccountForSession()`|\n|**Rate Limits**|Track rate limit status per account per model|`markRateLimited()`, `isRateLimited()`, `resetAllRateLimits()`|\n|**Credentials**|Manage OAuth tokens and project IDs|`getTokenForAccount()`, `getProjectIdForAccount()`|\n[...]\n/antigravity-proxy\n[...]\n## Account Selection Strategies\n[...]\nThe system implements two primary selection strategies, chosen based on whether a session ID is provided:\n[...]\n### Sticky Selection\n[...]\nSticky selection maintains the same account across conversation turns to maximize prompt cache hits. The session ID is derived by hashing the first user message:\n[...]\nIf the mapped account is rate-limited for the requested model, the system falls back to round-robin selection.\n[...]\n### Round-Robin Selection\n[...]\nRound-robin distributes load evenly across all available accounts. The `pickNext()` function:\n[...]\n1. Filters out invalid accounts (`isInvalid === true`)\n2. Filters out accounts rate-limited for the requested model\n3. Selects the next account in rotation\n4. Updates `lastUsed` timestamp\n5. Persists account state to `accounts.json`\n[...]\n## Rate Limit Tracking Per Model\n[...]\nEach account tracks rate limits separately for each model, enabling fine-grained quota management.\n[...]\n### Rate Limit Detection\n[...]\nWhen the CloudCode client receives a `429` or `RESOURCE\\_EXHAUSTED` error, it:\n[...]\n1. Parses the reset time from error message or headers (see src/cloudcode/rate-limit-parser.js)\n2. Calls `accountManager.markRateLimited(account, model, resetTime)`\n3. The rate limit is persisted to `accounts.json`\n4. The account becomes unavailable for that specific model until `resetTime`\n[...]\n### Automatic Cooldown\n[...]\nThe system automatically re-enables rate-limited accounts after their reset time expires:\n[...]\n## Automatic Account Switching\n[...]\nWhen a request encounters a rate limit, the system automatically attempts to switch to a different account.\n[...]\n### Max Wait Threshold\n[...]\nThe system uses a `MAX\\_WAIT\\_BEFORE\\_ERROR\\_MS` constant to determine switching behavior:\n[...]\n* **Short rate limits (≤ 2 minutes)**: Wait and retry with same account\n* **Long rate limits (> 2 minutes)**: Immediately switch to next available account\n[...]\n## Optimistic Retry Mechanism\n[...]\nWhen all accounts appear rate-limited for a given model, the system performs an optimistic retry before returning an error.\n[...]\n## Integration with Server\n[...]\nThe `AccountManager` is initialized at server startup and used throughout request processing.\n[...]\n|Location|Function|Purpose|\n|src/server.js23|`new AccountManager()`|Create singleton instance|\n|src/server.js33-54|`ensureInitialized()`|Lazy initialization with race protection|\n|src/server.js543-549|`isAllRateLimited()`, `resetAllRateLimits()`|Optimistic retry before sending request|\n|src/server.js602|`sendMessageStream()`|Pass `accountManager` to streaming handler|\n|src/server.js623|`sendMessage()`|Pass `accountManager` to message handler|\n[...]\nThe `ensureInitialized()` function provides race-condition protection for concurrent requests during startup, ensuring the account manager is fully loaded before processing any requests.\n[...]\n### GET /account-limits\n\n---\n\nTitle: GitHub - Three algorithms are available:\n[...]\nSmart (Default): Multi-factor scoring that considers:\n[...]\n- Cooldown state (profiles in cooldown are excluded)\n- Health status (prefers healthy profiles)\n- Recency (avoids profiles used in the last 30 minutes)\n- Plan type (slight preference for higher-tier plans)\n- Random jitter (breaks ties unpredictably)\n[...]\nRound Robin: Simple sequential rotation through profiles, skipping any in cooldown. Predictable and even distribution.\n[...]\nRandom: Purely random selection among non-cooldown profiles. Least predictable but may cluster usage.\n[...]\n### Cooldown Tracking\n[...]\nWhen an account hits a rate limit, you can mark it as \"in cooldown\" so rotation algorithms skip it:\n[...]\ncooldown enforcement is enabled (`stealth.cooldown.enabled: true`), attempting to activate a profile in cooldown will warn you and prompt for confirmation. When one account reaches its session or weekly rate limit, the system should **automatically switch to the next available account**.\n\n### Use Case\n\nWhen using AI providers like Claude / Claude Code, accounts often hit rate limits (session limits, weekly limits, etc.). Currently, this interrupts the workflow and requires manual intervention to switch accounts.\n\nWith multi-account support and automatic failover:\n\n- Users could configure multiple accounts (e.g., personal + work accounts)\n- When the primary account hits a limit, the system automatically uses the next account\n- This ensures uninterrupted workflow and better utilization of available quotas\n\n### Proposed Behavior\n\n1. Allow configuration of multiple accounts per provider (e.g., multiple Anthropic API keys or Claude accounts)\n2. Detect when an account reaches its rate limit (session/weekly/monthly)\n3. Automatically failover to the next configured account\n4. Optionally notify the user when a switch occurs\n5. Rotate back to the primary account when limits reset\n\n### Example Configuration (conceptual)\n\n```toml\n[providers.anthropic]\naccounts = [\n  { name = \"primary\", api_key = \"...\" },\n  { name = \"secondary\", api_key = \"...\" },\n]\nfailover = \"auto\"\n```\n\n### Benefits\n\n- Uninterrupted workflow during rate limits\n- Better utilization of multiple subscriptions/quotas\n- Improved developer experience\n\nThank you for considering this feature!\n\n---\n\n### Timeline\n\n**github-actions[bot]** assigned @thdxr · Jan 16, 2026 at 11:31am\n\n**@github-actions[bot]** commented · Jan 16, 2026 at 11:32am\n\n> This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. The 1% rule is bidirectional — even if uncertain whether skill X applies, invoke it; if it turns out wrong, drop it.\r\n\r\n### Default skill catalog by domain (1556 SKILL.md across 21 active plugins + 14 marketplaces)\r\n\r\nWhen uncertain which skill applies, the meta-skill `using-agent-skills` auto-fires and surfaces relevant skills via description matching. `.mcp.json` at the project root (project-scoped) or in `~/.claude.json` (user-scoped).\r\n\r\n### Server Types\r\n\r\n| Type | Transport | Example |\r\n|------|-----------|---------|\r\n| **stdio** | Spawns a local process | `npx`, `python`, binary |\r\n| **http** | Connects to a remote URL | HTTP/SSE endpoint |\r\n\r\n### Example `.mcp.json`\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\r\n  \"mcpServers\": {\r\n    \"context7\": {\r\n      \"command\": \"npx\",\r\n      \"args\": [\"-y\", \"@upstash/context7-mcp\"]\r\n    },\r\n    \"playwright\": {\r\n      \"command\": \"npx\",\r\n      \"args\": [\"-y\", \"@playwright/mcp\"]\r\n    },\r\n    \"deepwiki\": {\r\n      \"command\": \"npx\",\r\n      \"args\": [\"-y\", \"deepwiki-mcp\"]\r\n    },\r\n    \"remote-api\": {\r\n      \"type\": \"http\",\r\n      \"url\": \"https://mcp.example.com/mcp\"\r\n    }\r\n  }\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\nUse environment variable expansion for secrets instead of committing API keys in `.mcp.json`:\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\r\n  \"mcpServers\": {\r\n    \"remote-api\": {\r\n      \"type\": \"http\",\r\n      \"url\": \"https://mcp.example.com/mcp?token=${MCP_API_TOKEN}\"\r\n    }\r\n  }\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\n### Settings for MCP Servers\r\n\r\nThese settings in `.claude/settings.json` control MCP server approval:\r\n\r\n| Key | Type | Description |\r\n|-----|------|-------------|\r\n| `enableAllProjectMcpServers` | boolean | Auto-approve all `.mcp.json` servers without prompting |\r\n| `enabledMcpjsonServers` | array | Allowlist of specific server names to auto-approve |\r\n| `disabledMcpjsonServers` | array | Blocklist of specific server names to reject |\r\n\r\n### Permission Rules for MCP Tools\r\n\r\nMCP tools follow the `mcp__<server>__<tool>` naming convention in permission rules:\r\n\r\n```json\r\n{\r\n  \"permissions\": {\r\n    \"allow\": [\r\n      \"mcp__*\",\r\n      \"mcp__context7__*\",\r\n      \"mcp__playwright__browser_snapshot\"\r\n    ],\r\n    \"deny\": [\r\n      \"mcp__dangerous-server__*\"\r\n    ]\r\n  }\r\n}\r\n```\n\n### eee-mcp-json (2)\n{\n  \"_comment\": \"Wave 75 2026-05-08 — Tier-2A HTTP MCPs (github + context7 + deepwiki) + kits-convergence stdio ccbp-claude-memory-full\n….com/bcherny/status/2016339448863355206\"><img src=\"assets/claude-memory/claude-memory-monorepo.jpg\" alt=\"CLAUDE.md loading in monorepos\" width=\"600\"></a>\r\n</p>\r\n\r\n### The Two Loading Mechanisms\r\n\r\nClaude Code uses two distinct mechanisms for loading CLAUDE.md files:\r\n\r\n#### Ancestor Loading (UP the directory tree)\r\n\r\nWhen you start Claude Code, it walks **upward** from your current working directory toward the filesystem root and loads every CLAUDE.md it finds along the way. These files are loaded **immediately at startup**.\r\n\r\n#### Descendant Loading (DOWN the directory tree)\r\n\r\nCLAUDE.md files in subdirectories below your current working directory are **NOT loaded at launch**. They are only included when Claude reads files in those subdirectories during your session. This is known as **lazy loading**.\r\n\r\n### Example Monorepo Structure\r\n\r\nConsider a typical monorepo with separate directories for different components:\r\n\r\n```\r\n/mymonorepo/\r\n├── CLAUDE.md          # Root-level instructions (shared across all components)\r\n├── frontend/\r\n│   └── CLAUDE.md      # Frontend-specific instructions\r\n├── backend/\r\n│   └── CLAUDE.md      # Backend-specific instructions\r\n└── api/\r\n    └── CLAUDE.md      # API-specific instructions\r\n```\r\n\r\n### Scenario 1: Running Claude Code from the Root Directory\r\n\r\nWhen you run Claude Code from `/mymonorepo/`:\r\n\r\n```bash\r\ncd /mymonorepo\r\nclaude\r\n```\r\n\r\n| File | Loaded at Launch? | Reason |\r\n|------|-------------------|--------|\r\n| `/mymonorepo/CLAUDE.md` | Yes | It's your current working directory |\r\n| `/mymonorepo/frontend/CLAUDE.md` | No | Loaded only when you read/edit files in `frontend/` |\r\n| `/mymonorepo/backend/CLAUDE.md` | No | Loaded only when you read/edit files in `backend/` |\r\n| `/mymonorepo/api/CLAUDE.md` | No | Loaded only when you read/edit files in `api/` |\r\n\r\n### Scenario 2: Running Claude Code from a Component Directory\r\n\r\nWhen you run Claude Code from `/mymonorepo/frontend/`:\r\n\r\n```bash\r\ncd /mymonorepo/frontend\r\nclaude\r\n```\r\n\r\n| File | Loaded at Launch? | Reason |\r\n|------|-------------------|--------|\r\n| `/mymonorepo/CLAUDE.md` | Yes | It's an ancestor directory |\r\n| `/mymonorepo/frontend/CLAUDE.md` | Yes | It's your current working directory |\r\n| `/mymonorepo/backend/CLAUDE.md` | No | Different branch of the directory tree |\r\n| `/mymonorepo/api/CLAUDE.md` | No | Different branch of the directory tree |\r\n\r\n### Key Takeaways\r\n\r\n1. **Ancestors always load at startup** — Claude walks UP the directory tree and loads all CLAUDE.md files it finds. This ensures you always have access to root-level, repository-wide instructions.\r\n\r\n2. **Descendants load lazily** — Subdirectory CLAUDE.md files only load when you interact with files in those subdirectories. This prevents irrelevant context fr…\n\n…s regardless of project.\r\n\r\n### Why This Design Works for Monorepos\r\n\r\n- **Shared instructions propagate down** — Root-level CLAUDE.md contains repository-wide conventions, coding standards, and common patterns that apply ever…\n\n### ccbp-claude-startup-flags-full\n## Directory & Workspace\r\n\r\n| Flag | Short | Description
